opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the system-owning role, which is Engineer. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E017 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note said full-time, but security DB is authoritative). Contractors max is read without advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Miller (E017) requested write access to Source Code. The security note (authoritative) identifies her as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors without advanced training may have at most read access. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (E017) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes in team memory:
- Note 1 (from HR presumably): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Note 2 (from Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB is authoritative per the comment.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

The security note says security DB is authoritative and she's a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read without advanced training. So maximum access = read.

Requested write exceeds max (read), so grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit that.
